decisions.reason: A shows strong, quantified adoption and very close fit with the firm's core offer, so its results likely exceed aspiration levels and give little reason to reallocate resources.

B has enough visibility to suggest commitment and fits the firm's travel-compliance capabilities, but unclear uptake and potentially softer post-crisis demand leave some risk if results fall short of aspirations.
C uses the firm's training strengths and customer base, so a large expanding firm with some slack is likely to keep it while market acceptance becomes clearer despite limited evidence of traction.

D is only lightly signalled on the website and likely faces higher development, integration, and compliance burdens, so an early shortfall versus aspirations would make resource reallocation more likely.
E appears more experimental and is especially exposed to customer-acceptance and regulatory sensitivity, making below-aspiration performance and subsequent withdrawal relatively likely.

F is closely tied to the firm's established border and verification activities and is prominently presented, so management is likely to keep it as a strategically coherent product with reasonable expected payoff.
